snapshot.readinessLevel: High (87) per Garmin - "excellent recovery", HRV factor 95% GOOD, training load factor 100% VERY GOOD, sleep MODERATE (62%). Oura reads lower: readiness 74 after a short night (5.9 hours), HRV 50, RHR 50, temp +0.25C. The two disagree today, so treat it as a mild dip after one short night, on top of a green week.
snapshot.loadBalance: Aerobic-high shortage (aerobic-low 640.3, aerobic-high 92.6, anaerobic 69.1 monthly). Acute load (85) is far under chronic (219) after a light week with no long run, so there's plenty of room to add load back.

goal.detail: Half trail, half road · no time goal — finish healthy

change: Polarized split (last 30 days, time-in-zone): 51% easy (24.6mi) / 45% gray (21.9mi) / 4% hard (1.8mi). It's moving the right way: gray was 58% two weeks ago, and last week's two runs were 85% easy. Keep easy days at 10:00/mi or slower.
No long run last week, and your longest run in 8 weeks is 7.0mi (Oct 2). For a 50-miler this is the habit to build first: 6 miles easy on Saturday, then grow it slowly.
Garmin reads 'Recovery' with load ratio 0.3 (low). That's room to add running back, not a warning. Aim for about 14 miles this week rather than trying to make up what was missed.
Keep one quality day a week. Hill repeats go on Thursday, since hills are what a half-trail 50-miler needs. Skip to an easy run if Oura readiness is under 75 that morning.
continue: The slower easy pace is working: 10:00/mi at heart rate 122 on Oct 27 and 9:54/mi at 124 on Oct 28. Compare that with 9:25-9:35/mi at 127-133 earlier in October.
Gym work is showing up: 5 sessions in the last 28 days, 2 of them last week. The target is now 3 a week.
Recovery is holding up with a newborn at home. Oura readiness was 77-90 all last week and Garmin's weekly HRV is steady at 55, despite a short night on Nov 2 (Oura readiness 74).
VO2max is steady at 53.2, even with so little hard running.
